column3: The Hebrew says they assembled as one man; BSB says they gathered together.
The Hebrew leaves the reader unnamed and pictures listening as the ears of all the people directed to the book; BSB names Ezra and says they listened attentively.
The Hebrew calls the structure a wooden tower and says they made it, using an active plural; BSB says a high wooden platform built for the occasion.
The Hebrew places “and the Levites” after the names; BSB identifies all the named men as Levites at the beginning.
The Hebrew narrates their understanding of the reading; BSB describes the purpose that the people could understand it.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here; BSB names Nehemiah.
The Hebrew says all the people went to eat and drink; BSB says they began to eat and drink.
The Hebrew says “on the second day” without explicitly repeating “of the month,” which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew describes mediation through the hand of Moses; BSB says “through Moses.”
The Hebrew continues with instructions that they should announce the message; BSB narrates their proclaiming it.
The Hebrew names courtyards of God’s house in the plural; BSB says court in the singular.
The Hebrew leaves the reader and the plural feast-keepers unnamed; BSB names Ezra and the Israelites.
